rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Meccan sūra is chiefly a warning, opens with the moon-splitting sign and the deniers’ rejection, recalls judgment and ruined peoples, then closes with glad tidings for the pious.
rows.anchor: سورة ممحضة في الإنذار والتخويف إلا آيتين من آخرها تبشران المتقين بالجنة والحضور عند ربهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sūra is Meccan by its context; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī dismisses claims that it was revealed at Badr or that some verses are Medinan.
rows.anchor: والسورة مكية بشهادة سياق آياتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iqtirāb means an increase in nearness, so the Hour has drawn very near; al-sāʿa is the time when Resurrection occurs.
rows.anchor: الاقتراب زيادة في القرب فقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The moon split means it separated into two parts, becoming two segments.
rows.anchor: انفصل بعضه عن بعض فصار فرقتين شقتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse points to God’s sign of splitting the moon through the Prophet in Mecca before the Hijra, after Meccan polytheists requested it.
rows.anchor: تشير الآية إلى آية شق القمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports about the split are abundant, and hadith scholars and exegetes are said to have accepted them.
rows.anchor: وقد استفاضت الروايات على ذلك

rows.speaker: الحسن وعطاء والبلخي
rows.claim: Al-Hasan, ʿAṭāʾ, and al-Balkhī take the verse to predict a future split at the Hour, with past tense expressing certainty of occurrence.
rows.anchor: إلا الحسن وعطاء والبلخي حيث قالوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects the future-split reading: the next verse says they saw a sign, turned away, and called it persistent magic, which fits an event already shown to them.
rows.anchor: فإن سياقها أوضح شاهد على أن قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects identifying the verse with the modern theory that the moon separated from Earth: 54:2 describes people calling a manifest sign magic, and no one called that scientific fact magic.
rows.anchor: ما قيل إن الآية إشارة إلى ما ذهب إليه الرياضيون أخيرا أن القمر قطعة من الأرض

rows.speaker: جبير بن مطعم
rows.claim: Jubayr reports that the moon split at Mecca in the Prophet’s time into two parts, each appearing over a mountain; people accused Muhammad of magic, but one man said he could not bewitch everyone.
rows.anchor: عن جبير بن مطعم في قوله { وانشق القمر } قال انشق القمر ونحن بمكة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the event had already occurred before the Hijra and people saw the two halves.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله { اقتربت الساعة وانشق القمر } قال قد مضى ذلك قبل الهجرة

rows.speaker: حذيفة بن اليمان
rows.claim: In a sermon transmitted by Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī, Ḥudhayfa says the moon split in the Prophet’s time, the Hour is near, and worldly life is nearing its end; today is preparation and tomorrow the race.
rows.anchor: عن أبي عبد الرحمن السلمي قال خطبنا حذيفة بن اليمان بالمدائن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The split is reported through numerous routes from Anas, Ibn Masʿūd, Ibn ʿUmar, Jubayr, Ibn ʿAbbās, and Ḥudhayfa; al-Ālūsī also lists ʿAlī among the Companions who transmitted it.
rows.anchor: وقد روي انشقاق القمر بدعاء النبي

rows.speaker: السيد الشريف وابن السبكي
rows.claim: Al-Sayyid al-Sharīf and Ibn al-Subkī call the report mutawātir and say its mass transmission is beyond doubt.
rows.anchor: عن السيد الشريف في شرح المواقف وعن ابن السبكي في شرح المختصر أن الحديث متواتر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī notes the report’s standing among Sunni scholars and says its standing among Shiʿites was established earlier in the discussion.
rows.anchor: هذه حال الحديث عند أهل السنة وقد عرفت حاله عند الشيعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muslims accept the moon-splitting sign in Mecca before the Hijra at the polytheists’ request; Qur’an 54:2 and numerous reports from both groups support an actual event near revelation.
rows.anchor: آية شق القمر بيد النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم بمكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qur’an 54:2 requires that the moon split be a sign occurring near the time of revelation, which the polytheists rejected like other signs; proliferating reports from both Muslim groups also support it.
rows.anchor: فالآية الثانية تأبى إلا أن يكون مدلول قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an and Sunna establish the sign; splitting a celestial body is rationally possible, miracles can occur, and the event should be accepted though it is not among religion’s necessities.
rows.anchor: فالكتاب والسنة يدلان عليها وانشقاق كرة من الكرات الجوية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The objection reads Qur’an 17:59 as withholding signs because earlier peoples denied them, either predicting this community’s denial too or avoiding the annihilation that followed earlier rejection.
rows.anchor: مفاد الآية إما أنا لا نرسل بالآيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qur’an 17:59 concerns signs requested by people, not signs that support a messenger or wonders God grants graciously; the requested-sign policy addresses their expected denial and ensuing punishment.
rows.anchor: نعم هذا في الآيات المرسلة باقتراح من الناس دون الآيات التي تؤيد بها الرسالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The requested-sign objection is reinforced by Qur’an 17:90–93, where the people demand a spring from the earth and the Prophet is told to say he is only a human messenger.
rows.anchor: وقالوا لن نؤمن لك حتى تفجر لنا من الأرض ينبوعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet was sent to all humanity as the final prophet, as shown by Qur’an 7:158, 6:19, and 33:40.
rows.anchor: قل يا أيها الناس إني رسول الله إليكم جميعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At Mecca the Prophet faced hostility, abuse, mockery, and plots to expel or kill him, until God ordered the Hijra; many nevertheless believed while the larger public remained hostile.
rows.anchor: فقابلوه بما استطاعوا من الشقاق والإيذاء والاستهزاء وهموا بإخراجه أو إثباته أو قتله حتى أمره ربه بالهجرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qur’an 4:77, in a reported occasion of revelation, shows believers had asked permission to fight and were told to restrain themselves, indicating a community of some size despite persecution.
rows.anchor: كما يدل عليه قوله تعالى ألم تر إلى الذين قيل لهم كفوا أيديكم وأقيموا الصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the Hijra Islam spread through Medina, nearby regions, tribes, Yemen, and Arabia outside Mecca; in year six the Prophet wrote to rulers of Persia, Rome, and Egypt, and Mecca was conquered in year eight.
rows.anchor: ثم بسط الدعوة على غير الجزيرة فكاتب الملوك والعظماء من فارس والروم ومصر سنة ست من الهجرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Many Meccans converted between the Hijra and conquest, most converted at the conquest, and Islam continued to grow until its adherents numbered about one fifth of the earth’s population.
rows.anchor: وقد أسلم ما بين الهجرة والفتح جمع من أهلها وحواليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The requested split would entail punishment if denied, but the Prophet’s universal mission meant all humanity could not then be destroyed before the proof was complete; the event occurred five years before the Hijra.
rows.anchor: كانت آية انشقاق القمر آية اقتراحية تستعقب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qur’an 8:42 requires that destruction follow clear proof; Qur’an 48:25 says believers were among Mecca’s people, so God would not annihilate the city while they remained there.
rows.anchor: ما كان الله ليهلك جميع أهل مكة وحواليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God would not spare believers while annihilating disbelievers when many Meccans later accepted Islam, for Islam accepted outward profession; the obstinate leaders and mockers were the deniers described in Qur’an 2:6, and they were destroyed at Badr.
rows.anchor: وما كان الله سبحانه لينجي المؤمنين ويهلك كفارهم وقد آمن جمع كثير منهم فيما بين سنة خمس قبل الهجرة وسنة ثمان بعد الهجرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qur’an 17:59 cannot include signs supporting the mission or gracious wonders; if general, it restricts only requested signs, withheld because Quraysh would deny them and God did not wish to punish them immediately.
rows.anchor: فالآية لا تشمل قطعا الآيات المؤيدة للرسالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qur’an 8:33 says the Prophet’s presence and people’s seeking forgiveness prevented punishment; Qur’an 17:76 warns that expelling him would have brought their destruction soon afterward.
rows.anchor: وما كان الله ليعذبهم وأنت فيهم وما كان الله معذبهم وهم يستغفرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qur’an 8:34–35, revealed after Badr, shows there was no remaining barrier to punishment once the Prophet was gone; the Meccans then suffered the slaughter at Badr.
rows.anchor: والآيات تبين أنه لم يكن من قبلهم مانع من نزول العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Denial by earlier peoples and the Prophet’s presence restrained signs and immediate punishment; after grounds such as obstructing worship and mocking arose and he left, a sign could establish the case and punishment follow rejection.
rows.anchor: فإذا وجد مقتض للعذاب كالصد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qur’an 17:59 withholds signs while the Prophet is among the people; it does not rule out sending a sign and delaying punishment until after his departure. Badr itself was a sign and punishment.
rows.anchor: إنما يفيد الإمساك عن إرسال الآيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even if signs were withheld as useless before people predisposed to deny them, the moon split could prove the truth and falsehood could be undone, with punishment deferred until the Prophet left.
rows.anchor: فإن إرسالها مع تأخير العذاب والنكال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qur’an 17:93 does not deny prophetic miracles: that would contradict the Qur’an’s accounts of earlier miracles and the miraculous Qur’an itself; the Prophet means he cannot produce signs by himself, since their power belongs to God.
rows.anchor: فليس مدلوله نفي تأييد النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet says signs belong to God and come only by His will; Noah’s reply and Qur’an 13:38 likewise say a messenger brings a sign only by God’s permission.
rows.anchor: قل إنما الآيات عند الله وما يشعركم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An objection argues that a lunar split would have been seen everywhere and recorded by eastern and western astronomers, given its exceptional nature and the many incentives to transmit it.
rows.anchor: ومن الاعتراض على آية الانشقاق ما قيل إن القمر لو انشق كما يقال لرآه جميع الناس ولضبطه أهل الأرصاد في الشرق والغرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People may simply have missed the event; not every earthly or celestial occurrence is known, preserved, and inherited from one generation to the next.
rows.anchor: أن من الممكن أولا أن يغفل عنه فلا دليل على كون كل حادث أرضي أو سماوي معلوما للناس محفوظا عندهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabia had no observatory for celestial phenomena; observatories existed in India and western lands, but none is established for this time, reported as the first night of 14 Dhū al-Ḥijja, five years before the Hijra.
rows.anchor: أن الحجاز وما حولها من البلاد العربية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The moon was reportedly full, split briefly near sunset as it rose at Mecca, then rejoined; by the time it rose over western lands, it appeared whole.
rows.anchor: وقد كان القمر - على ما في بعض الروايات - بدرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He suspects non-Muslim church and polytheist adherents of withholding reports on religious matters that would benefit Islam.
rows.anchor: على أنا نتهم غير المسلمين من أتباع الكنيسة والوثنية في الأمور الدينية التي لها مساس نفع بالإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claim that gravity must fail for the halves to separate and thus they could never rejoin is unproved as a rational impossibility; if custom forbade rejoining, it should equally forbid splitting, and miracles break customary patterns.
rows.anchor: والجواب عنه أن الاستحالة العقلية ممنوعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This second section describes the second creation, return to God, and recompense, recalling divine favors; the preceding first section described the first creation and its favors.
rows.anchor: هذا هو الفصل الثاني من آيات السورة يصف نشأة الثقلين الثانية وهي نشأة الرجوع إلى الله وجزاء الأعمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To ‘be free for’ someone is to leave other tasks and focus attention on that matter; ‘We shall attend to you’ means the present creation will end and God will turn to the two groups.
rows.anchor: يقال فرغ فلان لأمر كذا إذا كان مشتغلا قبلا بأمور ثم تركها وقصر الاشتغال بذاك الأمر اهتماما به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The next verses explain this attention as resurrection, reckoning, and recompense for good or bad deeds; ‘attend to you’ is an implicit metaphor for the change of creation.
rows.anchor: وتبين الآيات التالية أن المراد بالاشتغال بهم بعثهم وحسابهم ومجازاتهم بأعمالهم خيرا أو شرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This ‘attending’ does not conflict with God’s not being distracted by one affair from another: it concerns a change of creation, while non-distraction concerns the reach of divine power; neither conflicts with God being in a new affair each day.
rows.anchor: ولا ينافي الفراغ لهم كونه تعالى لا يشغله شأن عن شأن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two weighty groups are jinn and humans; plural pronouns address them because each group contains many individuals.
rows.anchor: والثقلان الجن والإنس، وإرجاع ضمير الجمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address to jinn and humans is a challenge on Judgment Day: if able, escape through the regions of heaven and earth and leave God’s dominion and accountability.
rows.anchor: من خطابات يوم القيامة وهو خطاب تعجيزي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ability means power, escape through the regions means fleeing, and aqṭār is the plural of quṭr, meaning a direction or region; jinn are mentioned first because they move faster.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالاستطاعة القدرة، وبالنفوذ من الأقطار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Unless with authority’ means escape is possible only with some kind of dominion; sulṭān can mean existential power, proof or any argument, or kingship.
rows.anchor: أي لا تقدرون على النفوذ إلا بنوع من السلطة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative takes the denied escape as scientific penetration into the heavens and earth, but al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī says the context does not fit that reading.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد بالنفوذ المنفي في الآية النفوذ العلمي

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Rāghib defines shawāẓ as flame without smoke; al-Majmaʿ describes it as a green flame fragment breaking away from fire, close to that sense.
rows.anchor: اللهب الذي لا دخان فيه

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Majmaʿ glosses nuḥās as smoke, while al-Rāghib gives it as a flame without smoke; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī says the meaning is clear.
rows.anchor: والنحاس الدخان وقال الراغب هو اللهب بلا دخان والمعنى ظاهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘You will not help one another’ means they cannot support each other to escape the suffering, since causes lose their effect and there is no protector from God that day.
rows.anchor: أي لا تتناصران بأن ينصر بعضكم بعضا لرفع البلاء والتخلص عن العناء لسقوط تأثير الأسباب ولا عاصم اليوم من الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When heaven splits it becomes rose-red like red leather.
rows.anchor: أي كانت حمراء كالدهان وهو الأديم الأحمر

words: لَّا يُسْـَٔلُ عَن ذَنۢبِهِۦٓ إِنسٌۭ وَلَا جَآنٌّۭ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This verse and the following verses describe Judgment’s reckoning and reward, the condition of criminals, and those who fear their Lord’s station and their outcomes.
rows.anchor: الآية وما يتلوها من الآيات إلى آخر السورة تصف الحساب والجزاء

words: لَّا يُسْـَٔلُ عَن ذَنۢبِهِۦٓ إِنسٌۭ وَلَا جَآنٌّۭ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reckoning is swift, as Qur’an 14:51 says; the negated question is the familiar form of questioning and does not conflict with other verses that affirm questioning.
rows.anchor: ثم الآية تصف سرعة الحساب وقد قال تعالى والله سريع الحساب

words: لَّا يُسْـَٔلُ عَن ذَنۢبِهِۦٓ إِنسٌۭ وَلَا جَآنٌّۭ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question is denied at some stations, while other stations include questioning, sealed mouths, speaking limbs, and recognition by marks; hence Qur’an 37:24 and 15:92 do not contradict this verse.
rows.anchor: لأن اليوم ذو مواقف مختلفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sentence answers an implied question—if they are not asked their sins, what happens to them?—so it is set apart rather than coordinated with what precedes.
rows.anchor: في مقام الجواب عن سؤال مقدر كأنه قيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their sīmā is the conspicuous sign on their faces.
rows.anchor: والمراد بسيماهم علامتهم البارزة في وجوههم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nawāṣī is the plural of nāṣiya, the hair at the front of the head; aqdām is the plural of foot.
rows.anchor: والنواصي جمع ناصية وهي شعر مقدم الرأس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prepositional phrase bi-l-nawāṣī functions as the passive subject of yuʾkhadhu.
rows.anchor: وقوله { بالنواصي } نائب فاعل يؤخذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though no one is asked about sin, criminals are recognized by facial marks, seized by forelocks and feet, and cast into the Fire.
rows.anchor: يعرف المجرمون بعلامتهم الظاهرة في وجوههم فيؤخذ بالنواصي والأقدام من المجرمين فيلقون في النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The words ‘This is Hell’ through ‘boiling’ are the content of an omitted statement introduced by ‘it will be said’ on that day.
rows.anchor: مقول قول مقدر أي يقال يومئذ هذه جهنم التي يكذب بها المجرمون

rows.speaker: الطبرسي
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabrisī offers that, after God says they are seized by forelocks and feet, the Prophet says this is Hell denied by his people and they will enter it, so he need not grieve over them.
rows.anchor: وقال الطبرسي ويمكن أنه لما أخبر الله سبحانه أنهم يؤخذون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥamīm is hot water, and ān is water whose heat has reached its limit.
rows.anchor: والحميم الماء الحار، والآني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maqām is a verbal noun from qāma, annexed to its agent; God’s standing over a person’s deeds means encompassing and knowing them, preserving them, and recompensing them.
rows.anchor: والمقام مصدر ميمي بمعنى القيام مضاف إلى فاعله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He links God’s care and reckoning of each soul’s deeds to Qur’an 13:33.
rows.anchor: قال تعالى أفمن هو قائم على كل نفس بما كسبت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Meccan sūra depicts the Great Resurrection, its upheavals, the division of people into three groups, their outcomes, arguments against deniers, and death’s approach and final grouping.
rows.anchor: بيان تصف السورة القيامة الكبرى التي فيها بعث الناس وحسابهم وجزاؤهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sūra is Meccan, as indicated by the context of its verses.
rows.anchor: والسورة مكية بشهادة سياق آياتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wuqūʿ is the occurrence of an event; al-wāqiʿa can describe any event, but here means the event of Resurrection.
rows.anchor: وقوع الحادثة هو حدوثها، والواقعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Wāqiʿa is used as a standalone name for Resurrection, like al-Ḥāqqa, al-Qāriʿa, and al-Ghāshiya.
rows.anchor: وقد أطلقت إطلاق الأعلام كأنها لا تحتاج إلى موصوف مقدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional clause has no stated apodosis to magnify the event; its outcome is understood from the sūra’s account of people’s states, approximately that believers prosper and disbelievers lose.
rows.anchor: ولم يذكر جزاء الشرط إعظاما له وتفخيما لأمره

rows.speaker: المجمع
rows.claim: Al-Majmaʿ treats kādhiba as a verbal noun like ʿāfiya and ʿāqiba, so there is no falsehood in the event’s coming to pass.
rows.anchor: قال في المجمع الكاذبة مصدر كالعافية والعاقبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative parses kādhiba as an adjective with an omitted noun: there is no false report or case concerning its occurrence.
rows.anchor: وقيل كاذبة صفة محذوفة الموصوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khāfiḍa and rāfiʿa are two predicates whose subject is the pronoun referring to the Event.
rows.anchor: { خافضة رافعة } خبران مبتدأهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pair figuratively describes the Event overturning the visible world order: hidden realities emerge, causal traces are veiled, arrogant disbelievers are humbled, and the pious are exalted.
rows.anchor: وكونها خافضة رافعة كناية عن تقليبها نظام الدنيا المشهود فتظهر السرائر وهي محجوبة اليوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rajj means moving something with great force; the phrase points to the severe earthquake of the Hour.
rows.anchor: الرج تحريك الشيء تحريكا شديدا إشارة إلى زلزلة الساعة التي يعظمها الله سبحانه
